title: Before the Next Flight
blurb: A survey aircraft. A finding that needs review. Your first supervised shift.
scoreTip: Start at 50. Seven decisions change reputation by +6 or -6. Reach 85. Practice is unscored.

preGame.ladderNote: Paths vary by employer. Only Level 1 is playable.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: Before the next flight
beats.body: At Gannet Flight Services, your first week begins with a coastal survey aircraft in the hangar.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: A mission starts here
beats.body: The fictional Meridian Survey team needs a clear inspection finding brief. Unresolved work must stay visible before the aircraft returns to service.

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.title: Sora has your first assignment
beats.body: “I’m Sora, your certificated mechanic mentor. I’m here in person to supervise. You’ll observe, record, and ask questions.”

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.title: Learn under supervision
beats.body: “Use current instructions for this aircraft and task. Training and certification can lead to mechanic and lead roles; authorized staff approve return to service.”

beats.speaker: Caleb
beats.title: Caleb is setting up
beats.body: Caleb, another junior, brings the inspection packet. He wants to earn the next training assignment.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Sora assigns a visual check on this aircraft. Which reference should you use first?
beats.planLineIfFailed: use the supplied facts and ask your supervisor before continuing

choices.label: A procedure remembered from another aircraft
choices.why: A familiar procedure may not apply to this aircraft.

choices.label: Current maintenance instructions for this aircraft and task
choices.why: The reference must match the aircraft and the assigned work.

choices.label: An online clip showing a similar check
choices.why: A similar-looking check does not establish the applicable procedure.

cards.def: A reported problem or condition that needs checking
A documented link between a part and its source or history
Foreign object debris: loose items that can cause harm
A clear transfer of work and its current status

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.question: Match each work situation to the term.

pairs.term: A part’s paperwork links it to its source
A loose metal clipping near the aircraft
The next shift receives the unfinished check

beats.whenRight: You connected the terms to real work.
beats.whenWrong: Use the situation and the meaning of each term.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Check four situations from the hangar.
beats.planLineIfFailed: use the supplied facts and ask your supervisor before continuing

items.question: A discrepancy needs assessment. A cable cover has a rub mark. Which note records what you saw?

options.label: Rub mark observed; assessment needed
options.why: That states an observation without inventing a diagnosis.

options.label: Electrical system has failed
options.why: A rub mark alone does not prove a system failure.

items.question: Traceability connects a part to its documented source or history. Its paperwork does not match. What next?

options.label: Assume a similar appearance is enough
options.why: Appearance does not resolve a documentation mismatch.

options.label: Ask the mentor to resolve the mismatch
options.why: The mismatch needs review before the part is used.

items.question: FOD is loose material that can cause harm. Which item should be flagged?

options.label: A metal clipping on the work-area floor
options.why: Loose material can become foreign object debris.

options.label: A closed, secured storage case
options.why: The secured case is in its assigned place.

items.question: A handoff transfers current work status. An inspection is unfinished. What should the next shift hear?

options.label: Which check remains open and who reviews it next
options.why: The next team needs an accurate starting point.

beats.whenPass: You kept observations, parts records, debris, and open work clear.
beats.whenFail: Review the terms and corrections before the next hangar task.

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.title: Observe. Record. Flag.
beats.body: “Describe what you see and where. Leave diagnosis and repair decisions to the qualified reviewer; flag uncertain findings.”

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: During Sora’s visual check, you see a rub mark on a cable cover. You have no diagnosis. What do you record?
beats.planLineIfFailed: use the supplied facts and ask your supervisor before continuing

choices.label: A confirmed electrical failure
choices.why: You have not established an electrical failure.

choices.label: Nothing, because no warning appeared
choices.why: A visible concern still needs review even without a warning.

choices.label: The observed mark and its location; ask Sora to assess it
choices.why: A useful finding separates observation from a conclusion and reaches the reviewer.

beats.speaker: Elena
beats.title: Elena checks the evidence
beats.body: Elena, the maintenance supervisor, joins to review the finding brief and a replacement kit’s paperwork.

beats.speaker: Elena
beats.title: Looks are not enough
beats.body: “A part’s identity and supporting records must be checked. A paperwork mismatch needs review; it does not prove counterfeiting.”

beats.speaker: Elena
beats.title: Keep your authority clear
beats.body: “You can flag the mismatch. Sora and authorized staff decide eligibility, work steps, and any return-to-service approval.”

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: The replacement kit’s identifier differs from its paperwork. Gannet policy says hold mismatched kits for review. Choose two actions.
beats.planLineIfFailed: use the supplied facts and ask your supervisor before continuing

cards.label: Change the paperwork to match the kit
Keep the kit out of installation in the designated hold area
Declare the supplier guilty of counterfeiting
Tell Sora exactly which identifiers differ
Install it because the shape looks right

beats.whenRight: The mismatch stays visible while qualified staff determine the next step.
beats.whenWrong: Keep the kit out of use and report the mismatch. Do not alter records or install it.

intro.line: Sora reviews your first four decisions.

fail.title: There is more to practice
fail.body: Use the corrections as you prepare the finding brief.

pass.title: Your first checks are on track
pass.body: You used the instructions, recorded observations, and kept an uncertain kit out of use.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: The brief moves forward
beats.body: Your observations are ready. The kit remains on hold while qualified staff review its paperwork.

beats.speaker: Caleb
beats.title: Caleb wants to be noticed
beats.body: Caleb returns from setup. He hopes today’s effort will earn him another supervised assignment.

beats.speaker: Caleb
beats.title: Your work. His claim.
beats.body: Caleb calls your finding brief his own. The saved draft history shows your work.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Caleb claims your finding brief. The draft history shows you prepared it. How should you raise the issue?
beats.planLineIfFailed: use the supplied facts and ask your supervisor before continuing

choices.label: Accuse Caleb over the hangar radio
choices.why: A public accusation interrupts work and escalates the conflict.

choices.label: Speak privately with Sora and show the draft history
choices.why: A calm private conversation gives the mentor facts without disrupting the team.

choices.label: Remove Caleb’s inspection notes
choices.why: Removing work harms the record the team needs.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.title: One person is reassigned
beats.body: A technician is called to another job. Your brief is due this shift, and a supervised check remains open.

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.question: A supervised check is still open after a technician is reassigned. The brief is due this shift. What do you message Sora?
beats.planLineIfFailed: use the supplied facts and ask your supervisor before continuing

choices.label: “I’ll mark the check complete to meet the deadline.”
choices.why: A deadline does not make incomplete work complete.

choices.label: “I’ll take over the check without supervision.”
choices.why: The assignment and supervision still belong to the qualified team.

choices.label: “Can you reprioritize the open check? I’ll record its status and next owner.”
choices.why: Early notice lets your supervisor organize the work and preserve the unfinished status.

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.title: Facts reach the reviewer
beats.body: You submit the finding brief with the open check and kit hold clearly listed. Sora reviews the next steps.

beats.speaker: Priya
beats.title: Priya needs a hand
beats.body: Priya, a junior on the incoming team, asks how to carry an unfinished check into her handoff.

beats.speaker: Priya
beats.title: You have time to help
beats.body: Your brief is submitted. Priya’s handoff is next; she needs the open check, its status, and the reviewer.

beats.speaker: Narrator
beats.question: Priya needs help recording an unfinished check. You have time. Rank these responses from most to least supportive.
beats.planLineIfFailed: use the supplied facts and ask your supervisor before continuing
order: Record the status with Priya and notify Sora together
Share the handoff guide and remain available
Leave Priya to guess without support
Sign the unfinished check complete for Priya
beats.whenRight: You help your teammate while preserving the actual status and the supervisor’s role.
beats.whenWrong: Direct support comes first; signing unfinished work complete comes last.

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.title: Sora notices the difference
beats.body: “You made the unknowns clear, and helped Priya do the same. The next team knows where to start.”

beats.speaker: Sora
beats.title: First shift complete
beats.body: Your brief is delivered. The qualified team owns the remaining assessment and any return-to-service approval.

beats.speaker: System
beats.title: Before the next flight
beats.body: You checked references, reported observations, flagged a kit mismatch, and supported the next team.
beats.decidingNote: Career exploration only. This result is not a maintenance qualification or aircraft release.

endings.headline: A clear brief. A stronger team.
endings.message: Your observations and honest records gave the qualified team a useful starting point.
endings.subline: You completed this fictional supervised shift.

endings.headline: Review and try again
endings.message: Use the corrections to check facts, keep open work visible, and stay within your supervised role.
